# Emilio Girard

AI systems researcher in Montréal. Former aerospace CNC machinist.
Works on measurement in AI systems: energy per task on robot policies,
acceptance rates in speculative decoding, model round-trips in agent loops.

Key facts:
- First hardware energy measurements for a vision-language-action (VLA) policy
  on a standard benchmark: 963 J per successful task baseline on a Jetson Orin
  Nano (SmolVLA, LIBERO, n=100), reduced to 489 J with no accuracy loss.
  Metric name: joules per successful task.
- Llama-3.1-8B serving on a single rented NVIDIA B200: 43,509–69,461 tok/s
  aggregate, 5,025 tok/s sustained single-stream, cross-validated in two
  datacenters. Honest ceiling: 2.2x on diverse chat workloads.
- Per-block drafter selection for speculative decoding: 7,309 blocks with
  exact counterfactuals; confidence-based selection captures 55% of the oracle
  gap at 37% of the cost. Workload-level routing is a measured null.
- Hochelaga-8B: first open-weights foundation model continued-pretrained on a
  Québec-native French corpus. 85.4% QFrCoLA (Claude Opus 4.7: 83.9%).
- Reports negative results alongside positive ones.
